questions.stem: The table shows the names of some common pieces of laboratory apparatus used to make measurements.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table to show the name of the quantity that can be measured by each piece of apparatus, and a common unit used for that quantity. One example of each has been done for you.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which piece of apparatus is needed to make measurements in a paper chromatography experiment? A balance C ruler B gas syringe D stop clock

questions.stem: The table shows the names of some substances. It also shows whether each substance is an element or a compound, and the type of bonding in the substance.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table. One example of each has been done for you.

parts.label: b
parts.text: What is the formula of magnesium oxide? A $ \mathrm{M g_{2}O} $ B $ \mathrm{M g O} $ C $ \mathrm{M g O_{2}} $ D $ \mathrm{M g_{2}O_{2}} $

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which state symbol represents the physical state of hydrogen chloride at room temperature? A aq B g C l D s

questions.stem: The table shows the electronic configurations of four elements.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Why is argon an unreactive element?

parts.label: b
parts.text: Krypton is an unreactive element in the same group of the Periodic Table as argon, but in Period 4. It has an atomic number of 36. Deduce the electronic configuration of krypton. A 2.8.8.8 B 2.8.18.8 C 2.8.8.2.8.8 D 2.8.8.8.8.2

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calcium reacts with chlorine to form the ionic compound calcium chloride $ \mathrm{(C a C l_{2})}. $

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Describe, in terms of electrons, how an atom of calcium reacts with two chlorine atoms to form calcium chloride. You may use a diagram in your answer.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Write the formula of a calcium ion.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: In the reaction between calcium and chlorine, both oxidation and reduction occur. Which row shows the element that is oxidised and the element that acts as the reducing agent in this reaction?

parts.label: d
parts.text: A student uses a flame test to distinguish between separate samples of calcium chloride and potassium chloride. This is the student's method. There is one mistake in step 1 and one mistake in step 3. step 1 dip a platinum wire into some concentrated sodium hydroxide solution step 2 dip the platinum wire into the sample step 3 place the wire and sample into a luminous Bunsen flame step 4 record the colour of the flame Describe a correct method for step 1 and step 3. step 1. step 3.

parts.label: e
parts.text: What colour is the flame when the test on potassium chloride is carried out correctly? A green B lilac C orange D red

questions.stem: An industrial chemical company has supplies of ethene and ethanol. The company considers using these two processes. process 1 converting ethene to ethanol process 2 converting ethanol to ethene $\mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {4} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {6} \mathrm {O}$ A chemical equation for process 1 is

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which condition does the chemical company use in process 1? A aluminium oxide as a catalyst B a pressure of 65 atm C a temperature of $ 1 0 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ D sodium hydroxide as a solvent

parts.label: b
parts.text: The equation for process 1 shows the molecular formulae of ethene and ethanol. Draw the displayed formulae of ethene and ethanol.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Why is it correct to describe ethanol as saturated, but incorrect to describe it as a hydrocarbon?

parts.label: d
parts.text: A scientist working for the chemical company makes the following predictions that could affect processes 1 and 2 in the future: crude oil will be less available and more expensive the climate will be warmer and allow more sugar cane to be grown Suggest how each of these predictions would affect the two processes.

questions.stem: Potassium chloride, KCl, is very similar to sodium chloride, NaCl. They have the same type of crystal structure, and their aqueous solutions can be electrolysed to give similar products.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows part of the structure of potassium chloride. The plus (+) sign shows the position of one potassium ion. Complete the diagram using a plus (+) sign to show the position of each potassium ion, and a minus (-) sign to show the position of each chloride ion.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The diagram shows apparatus used to electrolyse aqueous potassium chloride in the laboratory.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Chlorine is formed at the positive electrode. Describe a test for chlorine gas.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Hydrogen gas is formed at the negative electrode. Write an ionic half-equation for the formation of hydrogen.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: The solution used in this electrolysis contains phenolphthalein. During the electrolysis, the colour of the solution around the negative electrode goes pink. Explain why the solution goes pink, and give the formula of the ion responsible for causing the colour change.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The ionic half-equation for the formation of chlorine at the positive electrode is $2 \mathrm {C l} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {C l} _ {2} + 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-}$ In one experiment a charge of 0.0250 faraday is passed through an aqueous solution of potassium chloride.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of chlorine formed.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Calculate the volume of chlorine formed at room temperature and pressure (rtp). [The molar volume of a gas is $ 2 4 \mathrm{~ d m}^{3} $ at rtp.] Give the unit in your answer.

questions.stem: A student prepares a solution of the soluble salt lithium sulfate, using the neutralisation reaction between sulfuric acid and the alkali lithium hydroxide. To make sure that she obtains a pure solution of the salt, she first carries out a titration to find the volumes of sulfuric acid and lithium hydroxide that react exactly together. She uses this method in the titration. use a pipette to add 25.0 $ cm^{3} $ of dilute sulfuric acid to a conical flask add a few drops of phenolphthalein indicator fill a burette with lithium hydroxide solution add the lithium hydroxide solution from the burette until the indicator just changes colour

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows the burette readings in the experiment before and after adding the lithium hydroxide solution. Use these readings to complete the table, giving all values to the nearest 0.05 $ cm^{3}. $

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student repeats the experiment using a different concentration of sulfuric acid The table shows her results. The average (mean) volume of alkali should be calculated using only concordant results. Concordant results are those volumes that differ from each other by 0.20 $ cm^{3} $ or less.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Identify the titration results to be used by placing ticks ( $ \checkmark $ ) in the table where appropriate.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Use the titration results you ticked in (i) to calculate the average (mean) volume of alkali added.

parts.label: c
parts.text: In a titration using solutions of the same acid and alkali but of different concentrations, she recorded these results. volume of sulfuric acid = 25.0 $ cm^{3} $ concentration of sulfuric acid = 0.107 mol/dm $ ^{3} $ average (mean) volume of lithium hydroxide solution = 22.85 $ cm^{3} $ The equation for the reaction is $2 \mathrm {L i O H} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} \rightarrow \mathrm {L i} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of $ \mathrm{H_{2} S O_{4}} $ in $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of $ 0. 1 0 7 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ sulfuric acid. $\mathrm {a m o u n t o f H _ {2} S O _ {4}} =$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of LiOH in the $ 2 2. 8 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of lithium hydroxide solution. $\mathrm {a m o u n t o f L i O H} =$

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm $ ^{3} $ , of LiOH in the lithium hydroxide solution. $\mathrm {c o n c e n t r a t i o n o f L i O H} =$

parts.label: d
parts.text: To prepare the solution of lithium sulfate, the student mixes together the volumes of acid and alkali obtained from the titration results. She then tests a sample of the lithium sulfate solution formed by adding a few drops of barium chloride solution.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Describe the observation she makes.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: State the name of the substance responsible for this observation.

questions.stem: A student investigates the temperature rise of water in a copper can placed above a spirit burner containing a flammable liquid. The diagram shows the apparatus he uses. This is the student's method. place 200 g of water in the copper can and record the temperature of the water weigh the spirit burner containing the flammable liquid place the spirit burner underneath the copper can and light the burner after two minutes extinguish the flame and record the maximum temperature of the water reweigh the spirit burner containing the remaining flammable liquid

parts.label: a
parts.text: State whether each of the changes listed in the table would increase, decrease or have no effect on the value of the maximum temperature of the water.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In one experiment pentane was used as the flammable liquid. The calculated heat energy change was 51900 J. In the experiment the mass of pentane burned was 1.88 g. The relative molecular mass of pentane is 72 Use this information to calculate the molar enthalpy change of combustion, in kJ/mol, of pentane.
